title: India Eye Series Clinch in Hamilton as Injury-Hit New Zealand Fight to Stay Alive
excerpt: Up 2-0 after two bowling-led wins, Shubman Gill's side can settle the five-match series at Seddon Park on Tuesday — and for fans in the US, the first ball is Monday night on Willow TV.
body:
• India, leading the five-match ODI series 2-0, can clinch it with a win over New Zealand in the third ODI at Seddon Park, Hamilton, on Tuesday, November 10.
  • For US viewers the first ball is Monday night: 9:00 p.m. ET / 6:00 p.m. PT on Willow TV. In India it is 7:30 a.m. IST on Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV.
  • New Zealand are injury-hit: Lockie Ferguson is out with a right-calf tear and Blair Tickner misses the next two matches under a seven-day stand-down after a blow to his helmet.
  • India's bowlers have set up both wins so far — New Zealand were restricted to 185 in Auckland and 134 in Wellington, where Gurnoor Brar took a career-best 4 for 30.

India will look to wrap up the five-match ODI series with two games to spare when they take on New Zealand in the third match at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday, IANS reported. Leading 2-0 after back-to-back victories in rain-affected matches in Auckland and Wellington, Shubman Gill's side can settle the series, while Mitchell Santner's hosts — who also lost the preceding T20I series 2-3 — must win to keep the contest alive.

How the series has gone

India's bowling attack has been the defining factor. New Zealand were restricted to 185 in the opening ODI, where Virat Kohli's 74 provided the foundation for the chase, and managed only 134 in Wellington, where Gurnoor Brar delivered a match-winning, career-best spell of 4 for 30, with Anshul Kamboj and Axar Patel also contributing. India's batting has been less convincing: in the second match the visitors slipped to 113 for 7 before rain intervened, and KL Rahul's unbeaten 26 proved crucial in keeping India just four runs ahead on the DLS par score.

For New Zealand, Daryl Mitchell's 55 in the second ODI and Santner's 31 were rare positives. Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips will need to give the middle order a platform it has not had so far.

"India will look to wrap up the five-match ODI series with two games to spare when they take on New Zealand in the third match at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday, IANS reported."

Team news

New Zealand's preparations have been disrupted by injuries. Lockie Ferguson has been ruled out with a right-calf tear, while Blair Tickner will miss the next two matches after taking a blow to his helmet in Wellington and being placed under the mandatory seven-day stand-down protocol. Kristian Clarke has been brought into the squad as cover, and New Zealand announced different squads for the third and fourth ODIs on Monday, with the squad for the fifth match to be named later.

New Zealand squad: Mitchell Santner (captain), Michael Bracewell, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Kyle Jamieson, Nick Kelly, Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith, Will Young.

India squad: Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (captain), Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj, Mohammed Siraj, Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Ishan Kishan.

When and where to watch

The match starts at 3:00 p.m. local time in Hamilton on Tuesday, November 10 — 7:30 a.m. IST. In the United States, that is Monday, November 9 at 9:00 p.m. ET and 6:00 p.m. PT, live on Willow TV. In India, the match is on Sony Sports Network with streaming on SonyLIV, and Wisden reports Doordarshan Sports will also carry the series on DD Free Dish. Viewers in New Zealand can watch on Sky Sport.

A win for India seals the series 3-0 with two matches to play. A win for New Zealand keeps it alive and shifts the pressure back onto a visiting side whose batting, unlike its bowling, has not yet fired in this series.
